item.title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial arbitrage pricing theory (S-APT) extends factor models to allow returns to spill over between connected firms, beyond what common risk factors explain. In recent years, tabular foundation models (TFMs) have matched or outperformed tuned gradient-boosted and bagged ensembles on small and medium-sized tabular benchmarks. Although their predictive performance is strong, these models reveal little about what they have learned, which limits their use in regulated financial applications that require explanation. Internal representations are widely used to probe what neural networks learn and to measure similarity. In this paper, we use the frozen representations of four TFMs as a measure of financial dissimilarity in a spatial asset-pricing model of US equities from 2011 to 2025, and find that their estimated gains over a direct distance between the same disclosures become consistently positive once broad SEC filing data are included. This reframes tabular foundation models from black-box predictors into instruments for measuring economic structure, with immediate applications to peer selection, risk attribution and network-based asset pricing. More broadly, our findings suggest that the internal representations of foundation models, not only their predictions, deserve study as economic objects, opening a new line of research on what pretrained models know about firms.

item.title: Conditional Deep Levy Models for Exotic Derivatives: History-Aware Path Generation and P-Q Payoff Diagnostics
item.description: arXiv:2509.13374v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a history-aware equity-index path generator based on Denoising Levy Probabilistic Models (DLPMs) and evaluate its predictive distributions through path-dependent derivative payoffs. A conditional U-Net combines contract state, index identity, 60- and 252-day return histories, and financial regularization with coordinate-wise stable mixing. A matched experiment holds initialization, training data, batch order, objective, computational budget and evaluation checkpoint fixed while comparing $\alpha=1.9$ with the Gaussian limit $\alpha=2$. On 6,824 chronological windows from eight Chinese and U.S. indices, terminal CRPS falls from 0.050585 to 0.048031, a 5.05% reduction, and path energy improves by 4.03%. The paired 60-calendar-day CRPS interval is [-0.004022, -0.001298]. Coverage rises from 56.68% to 71.00% while the proper 90% interval score improves by 20.30%. Empirical references remain competitive: the full-pool terminal control attains CRPS 0.047566. A common P-Q protocol translates the forecasts into vanilla, Asian and floating-strike lookback outcomes against an independent martingale-corrected Student-t GARCH benchmark. With quote-error filtering and a fixed-state initial Delta hedge, the matched Lookback difference is 0.285% of initial spot, with a 60-day interval [0.061%, 0.489%]. The evaluation also applies the same recorded ensembles to accumulator and snowball scenarios. These contracts expose different responses of early termination and downside cashflows to the noise specification. The study connects conditional historical path generation, a controlled stability-parameter comparison, empirical forecasting references, and payoff-sensitive derivative evaluation.
